content.text: {"headline":"No action needed: hold the current plan (P0). Service level is predicted at 94.1% for 13:45–15:45, well above the 80% target, at no extra cost.","why":"The morning dip was caused by slow handle time on Payments, not extra calls or absences. Handle time jumped to 479 s at 11:15 against 313 s forecast, and service level fell as low as 1.8% at 11:45. This most likely came from the CardMax slowness reported in INC-20261019-1835 after this morning's release. That ticket is now resolved and handle time is recovering: 391 s at 13:15 and 340 s at 13:30. With no changes, Payments is predicted at 92.9% and General at 95.6% for 13:45–15:45. Abandons are predicted at 1.3% and rest of day at 96.5%, so intervening is not needed to meet target.","trade_offs":["P2 (move 1 cross-skilled agent from General to Payments, plus chat deflection) scores slightly higher at 95.9% for INR 564. The gain is small when P0 already clears target comfortably. It also takes a person off General, though General is still predicted at 97.5% under P2.","P1 (delayed breaks plus IVR callback) and P3 (overtime plus delayed breaks) cost nothing extra, but both predict worse results than doing nothing. Each comes in at 92.5% with higher abandons (2.2% and 2.1% vs 1.3%), and they disrupt agents' breaks for no benefit."],"watch":"Payments handle time should keep heading back toward the ~313 s forecast. Because the CardMax link is likely but not proven, recheck if handle time climbs back above ~400 s or the incident is reopened. If that happens, P2 is the ready fallback."}
